must_haves: security and where data is stored (Stockholm)

layout.idea: Sticky split: left 5 columns hold headline and Start free pinned; right 7 columns scroll through four screenshots in order (connect, paste URL, ask, approve).
layout.why: The CTA never leaves the screen while the four real steps play out beside it.

hero.idea: Install hero: two equal columns 'Add to Claude' and 'Add to ChatGPT', each with three numbered steps and a screenshot, Start free above both.
hero.why: Most visitors already chose their AI client; meet them there.

visual_style.idea: Hardware labels: light grey panels with tiny uppercase labels in ink and cobalt status dots, like markings on a device.
visual_style.why: Gives the connector a tangible, engineered feel.

typography.idea: Source Serif 4 600 at opsz 60 for a 72px display, Public Sans 400 body, Public Sans 700 for labels.
typography.why: Government-plain body under a confident serif.

narrative.idea: Interview: the page as a Q and A with the maker; questions in bold, short honest answers.
narrative.why: Conversational, human, answers objections in passing.

proof.idea: Real customer quotes only, each with a name and a link to where it was published; the section is hidden when there are none approved.

asset_use.idea: Diagrams in the margin: small line diagrams sit in the right margin next to the paragraph they explain.
asset_use.why: Diagrams support the text instead of interrupting it.

motion.idea: Hovering a provider logo reveals how it connects (OAuth or app password) in a small label below it.

section_order.idea: Hero clip > Connect (providers) > Paste URL (clients) > Ask > Approve > Sent > Pricing > FAQ
section_order.why: The page is the setup sequence.

voice.idea: Calm Scandinavian understatement. Sample: 'It reads your mail when you ask, and keeps none of it.'
voice.why: Matches Stockholm and a privacy-first product.

wildcard.idea: Lowercase everywhere except product and provider names.
wildcard.why: A distinct, quiet voice in type.
